map.Lessons 6-6, 6-7 & 6-8 — equivalent expr: Lessons 6-6, 6-7 & 6-8: equivalent expressions, GCF & LCM, and the distributive property. The finale of the cipher vault.
map.Previously: the reader dialed the power: Last time: the reader set the power ring right. Exponents tamed. Order of operations restored. One sealed chamber remains.
map.Previously, in Episode 2: the power ring: Last time, in Episode 2: the power ring spun, locked, and held. Beyond it waits Ada Vex's last chamber, and the glitch's last stand.
map.Two doors, one lock. Ada's plaque says t: Two doors, one lock. Ada's plaque says they open only when both faces show the SAME value, for every number you feed them.
map.Not \"look the same.\" BE the same. x +: Not "look the same." BE the same. x + x and 2x: pick any x you want, both faces match. Those are real twins.
map.Equivalent expressions name the same val: Equivalent expressions give the same value for EVERY value of the variable. Twins in different jackets.
map.One jacket-swap tool: the distributive p: One jacket-swap tool is the distributive property: a(b + c) = ab + ac. The outside number multiplies BOTH terms inside.
map.The glitch slithers across the right-han: The glitch slides across the right-hand door. Plates flicker. Some of these "twins" are… off.
map.It's running a disguise meta — fake twin: It's running a disguise game: fake twins that match at ONE number and differ at all the others.
map.So we test like scientists: feed both fa: So we test like scientists: feed both faces y = 1, then y = 3. One disagreement unmasks a fake. Or distribute and combine like terms: terms with the same variable part add together.
map.Algebra unmasks disguises faster than lu: Algebra unmasks disguises faster than luck: distribute, combine like terms, THEN decide.
map.Reader — stamp all four pairs. The glitc: Reader, stamp all four pairs. The glitch only needs ONE wrong stamp to keep the doors shut.
map.Four pairs of door-plates glow. Tap a pa: Four pairs of door-plates glow. Tap a panel to stamp it: first tap EQUIV (true twins, equal for EVERY y), second tap NOT (a disguise), third tap clears. All four stamps must be correct at once.
map.Conceptual: true twins agree for EVERY v: Conceptual: true twins agree for EVERY value of y. Feed both plates y = 1, then y = 3. A single disagreement unmasks a disguise.
map.Procedural: distribute parentheses and c: Procedural: distribute the parentheses and combine like terms before you decide. a(b − c) = ab − ac. The multiplier must hit BOTH terms inside. And adding copies is a different move from multiplying them.
map.I could build this. The link-cog has to: I could build this. The link-cog has to mesh BOTH gears. Its tooth count must divide 18 and 30 exactly. The biggest one that fits.
map.GCF: the greatest factor two numbers sha: GCF: the greatest factor two numbers share. LCM: the first multiple both counting lists share.
map.Factors divide IN — a GCF never beats ei: Factors divide IN. A GCF is never bigger than either number. Multiples count UP. An LCM is never smaller than either.
map.Two locks hold the corridor. Cog lock: t: Two locks hold the corridor. Cog lock: the link-cog's tooth count is the GCF of 18 and 30, the greatest count that divides both gears. Beacon lock: door-lights blinking every 4 turns and every 10 turns first flash together at their LCM. After how many turns?
map.Conceptual: a GCF divides INTO both numb: Conceptual: a GCF divides INTO both numbers, so it can never be bigger than either gear. An LCM is counted UP TO, so it can never be smaller than either blink number. Factors divide in. Multiples count up.
map.Procedural: list every factor of 18 and: Procedural: list every factor of 18 and every factor of 30. Keep the greatest one both lists share. For the beacons, skip-count by 4s and by 10s until both lists reach the same number.
map.The keyway won't take the engraving as w: The keyway won't take the engraving as written. It wants the factored twin, with the greatest common factor out front.
map.To expand, push the multiplier through t: To expand, push the multiplier through the parentheses. To factor, pull the GCF back out. Same hallway, walked in both directions.
map.Andre's warm-up: 9m + 12. GCF of 9 and 1: Andre's warm-up: 9m + 12. The GCF of 9 and 12 is 3, so it factors to 3(3m + 4). Distribute to check. It snaps right back.
map.Ada's engraving reads 12x + 30. The keyw: Ada's engraving reads 12x + 30. The keyway only accepts its factored twin: greatest common factor out front, nothing left to pull.
map.Conceptual: factoring runs the distribut: Conceptual: factoring runs the distributive property in REVERSE. Pull the greatest common factor out front. What stays inside must multiply back to the original, term by term.
map.Procedural: find the GCF of 12 and 30 fi: Procedural: find the GCF of 12 and 30 first. Then divide EACH term by it. The x-term fills the first blank inside. The constant fills the second. Distribute to check your key.
map.The key turns. And the glitch panics — s: The key turns. And the glitch panics, swelling until it floods BOTH doors at once.
map.Final boss. It's mirroring — one door wa: Final boss. It's mirroring: one door wants factoring, the other wants expanding. Both directions at once.
map.And a seal between them demands a REASON: And a seal between them demands a REASON. Equivalence is never a feeling. It is a property.
map.Six units of grinding for this moment. R: Six units of grinding for this moment. Reader, you're my co-op partner. Let's finish this.
map.Boss Gate: factor one door, expand the o: Boss Gate: factor one door, expand the other. Then stamp WHY your twins are guaranteed true.
map.The glitch floods both doors at once. Th: The glitch floods both doors at once. Three locks. Lock 1: the left door wants the factored twin of 16a + 40, GCF out front. Lock 2: the right door wants the expanded twin: 7(3n + 2). Lock 3: stamp the seal. Say WHY the doors must accept your twins.
map.Conceptual: factoring and expanding are: Conceptual: factoring and expanding are the SAME distributive property walked in opposite directions: a(b + c) = ab + ac. A twin is guaranteed when a property builds it, not when one lucky number agrees.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — GCF of 16 and 40 fi: Procedural: Lock 1: find the GCF of 16 and 40 first, then divide each term by it. Lock 2: the multiplier must hit BOTH terms inside the parentheses. Lock 3: pick the reason that covers EVERY value of the variable.
map.And THAT — that's Ada's engine room. The: And THAT is Ada's engine room. The whole story starts in there.
map.The cipher vault, the glitch's origin, a: The cipher vault, the glitch's start, and the master key, from fraction division to the distributive property, all in the anchor book.
map.Equivalent expressions.Twins name the sa: Equivalent expressions.Twins give the same value for EVERY value of the variable. One disagreement, at any number, unmasks a fake.
map.Distributive property.a(b + c) = ab + ac: Distributive property.a(b + c) = ab + ac. The multiplier hits BOTH terms inside. Skipping one makes a disguise, not a twin.
map.Factor & expand.Expand pushes the multip: Factor & expand.Expand pushes the multiplier through the parentheses. Factor pulls the GCF back out front. Same hallway, both directions.
map.GCF & LCM.GCF: greatest factor two numbe: GCF & LCM.GCF: the greatest factor two numbers share. It divides IN. LCM: the first multiple their lists share. It counts UP.
map.completed Unit 6 · Episode 3: The Twin D: finished Unit 6 · Episode 3: The Twin Doors and showed mastery of equivalent expressions, GCF & LCM, and factoring with the distributive property.
map.The full story — Vol. 6: The Expression: The full story, Vol. 6: The Expression Engine, is waiting beyond the doors.
map.Pair to judge: 4(x + 3) vs 4x + 12. Dist: Pair to judge: 4(x + 3) vs 4x + 12. Distribute: 4·x + 4·3 = 4x + 12. Identical. True twins.
map.Pair: 3(x − 5) vs 3x − 5. Distribute: 3x: Pair: 3(x − 5) vs 3x − 5. Distribute: 3x − 15, which is NOT 3x − 5. The 3 must multiply the 5 as well. Disguise.
map.Pair: m + m + m vs 3m. Adding three copi: Pair: m + m + m vs 3m. Adding three copies makes 3 OF them. Twins. MULTIPLYING three copies would be m³, a very different thing.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Different corridor: gears of 12 and 20 t: New corridor: gears of 12 and 20 teeth. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Greatest shared factor: 4.
map.Its beacons blink every 3 turns and ever: Its beacons blink every 3 turns and every 5 turns. Skip-count: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, … and 5, 10, 15, … The lists first meet at 15. LCM = 15.
map.Sanity rails: a GCF is never bigger than: Sanity checks: a GCF is never bigger than either gear. An LCM is never smaller than either blink count. If your answers break these, you swapped them.
map.Why guaranteed twins? The distributive p: Why guaranteed twins? The distributive property holds for EVERY value, so the two forms can never disagree. One lucky test is a clue. The property is proof.
map.Every plate needs a stamp — EQUIV or NOT: Every plate needs a stamp: EQUIV or NOT.
map.90 is a common MULTIPLE of 18 and 30 — t: 90 is a common MULTIPLE of 18 and 30. The cog wants the greatest common FACTOR. A factor can't be bigger than the gears it divides.
map.2 is the greatest common FACTOR of 4 and: 2 is the greatest common FACTOR of 4 and 10. The beacon lock wants their first common MULTIPLE. Count UP, not in.
map.40 is a shared multiple, but the beacons: 40 is a shared multiple, but the beacons sync sooner. Think LEAST common multiple.
map.Cog: GCF = 6 teeth. Beacons: LCM = 20 tu: Cog: GCF = 6 teeth. Beacons: LCM = 20 turns. KA-CHUNK! The corridor seal opens!
map.12x + 30 = 6(2x + 5). The key glows ambe: 12x + 30 = 6(2x + 5). The key glows amber, turns, and the third seal opens!
map.Your key multiplies back to the engravin: Your key multiplies back to the engraving, but a common factor still hides inside the parentheses. The keyway wants the GREATEST factor out front.
map.Lock 1 holds. It multiplies back, but a: Lock 1 holds. It multiplies back, but a common factor still hides inside the parentheses. Pull the GREATEST one out front.
map.Lock 2 holds. The 7 multiplied the 3n bu: Lock 2 holds. The 7 multiplied the 3n but skipped the +2. Distribute to BOTH terms.
map.Lock 2 holds. 7 + 3 is not how distribut: Lock 2 holds. 7 + 3 is not how distributing works. The 7 MULTIPLIES each term inside.
map.Two locks open! Stamp the seal — choose: Two locks open! Stamp the seal. Choose the reason your twins are guaranteed.
map.Lock 3 holds. One match can be luck — th: Lock 3 holds. One match can be luck. The glitch makes fakes that agree at a single number. Twins must agree EVERYWHERE.
map.Lock 3 holds. 3(c − 2) and 3c − 2 use th: Lock 3 holds. 3(c − 2) and 3c − 2 use the same numbers but are NOT twins. Position changes meaning. You need a property, not a shuffle.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
